scope: Check prepared browser exports before handing off downloads; restore generation on expiry, retain retryable packages after transient failures, and cancel stale handoffs without revoking active downloads

before.sourceState: Final test replayed against the prior browser controller, client, English catalogue and HTML in an isolated copy; N107 server changes retained. Restored production fingerprints match the previous snapshot and release baseline.
before.reproduction: Old download anchor handed the URL off immediately, never checked availability and had no cancellation/retry state for such a check; both actual HTTP controller cases observed no preflight request. The added malformed-probe case confirms the missing client guard.

initialFocusedRun.failure: Eleven new test teardown hooks compared textarea content to CRLF source rather than the LF-normalized display value; all functional assertions reached cleanup.
initialFocusedRun.resolution: Snapshot the textarea value immediately after assignment and compare it after the workflow. Disk and ZIP byte comparisons remain unchanged; final replay uses the corrected test.

application.skipReason: Native archive interoperability and registry agreement require VIENTO_TEST_ARCHIVE_BINARY; prior b.4.0 native evidence retained.

commands.after: /usr/bin/node --test scripts/tests/export-browser.test.mjs scripts/tests/editor-dialogs.test.mjs scripts/tests/export-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/export-downloads.test.mjs scripts/tests/export.test.mjs scripts/tests/export-cleanup.test.mjs scripts/tests/request-lifecycle.test.mjs scripts/tests/i18n.test.mjs

testEnvironment: Production controllers in event-capable DOM fixtures; real export client and edit/browse HTTP servers on synthetic projects; actual in-app browser downloads with SHA-256 comparison to server staging files. No daily workspace data accessed.
limitations: A validity probe and the following browser download are separate requests. Service exit or external deletion between them remains a browser transfer failure.
DOM error/cancellation races are controlled in automated tests; actual browser smoke covers successful download, unavailable job recovery and repeated download.
Native windows, Rust archive tests and media decoding were not rerun.
